profile.headline: Software Engineer @Thales
profile.summary:
Hi! I am currently a software engineer at Thales where I develop entertainment for customer airlines! My responsibilities include designing, testing, deploying, and maintaining the front-end of customer entertainment systems. In a gist, I work on the UI components of the system using Qt QML, Javascript, and MySQL, and use C++ and Java to embed the system into Thales Android-based devices. 

I've always loved leading and learning in tech, feel free to reach out and connect! :)

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Implement, test, and maintain new customer GUI features in Qt QML/C++ by aligning to product requirements, directing SCRUM standups to identify functional issues, and designing solutions by peer consultation.
- Write customer-specific Android apps and C++ plugins to overlay the Qt QML GUI and improve app performance.
- Develop reusable features and fixes on the Qt C++ backend by using JNI to expose low-level Android APIs, designing new interfaces for Qt QML use, and writing simulated environments and tests to verify functionality.
- Coordinate with external teams to design feature architecture, integrate proper test environments, and debug product defects to meet recurring customer deadlines.

positions.title: Android Tech Fellow
positions.description: Directed CodePath.org's 15-week Android Mobile Development course at Cal Poly Pomona through coordination with supervisor and grading teams. Included hosting weekly lecture, lab, and live coding sessions to facilitate Android project-based assignments.

positions.title: Android Technical Assistant
positions.description: Troubleshooted Android bugs for all cohorts of CodePath.org's Android Mobile Development course around the US. Debugged and unblocked student learning through providing one-on-one help over Zoom, Slack, and CodePath.org's discussion system.

positions.title: Android Intern Lead (IL)
positions.description: Mentored Meta interns over Summer 2021 as Android expert and project manager. Facilitated Android assignments and hosted instructional and team-building exercises. Guided interns through the App Development Lifecycle and SCRUM to build and demo their first original Android apps by the end of the program.

positions.title: Team Leader and Trainer
positions.description:
- Operated store location by cooperating with Kitchen Team Leader, handling up to $2,750/hr profits with 37+ employees at a time, while completing Drive-Thru order transactions at a 5 minute average.
- Weekly reported and analyzed Drive-Thru Accuracy and Customer Service scores to Leadership Team, and proposed policy on employee rotation hours, overall affecting weekly scores by +/- 5%.
- Trained 10+ new employees on Chick-fil-A specific hard and soft skills, such as GROWTH and Core 4

honors.title: 2nd Place Android Mobile App
honors.description:
My group's Android app, Wings, was honored the 2nd place title at National CodePath Android Demo Day - 2021. For more detail, Wings is listed in the Projects section!

This event is a competition between the Top 10 Android applications (determined by a preliminary event) made by CodePath.org students during the Spring running of the course. Each group competitor leads a 3 min demo of their app to a panel of industry professionals acting as judges.

This year's judges:
- Alice Yuan – Senior Software Engineer at Odeko
- Caren Chang – Android Engineer at Google
- Dan Ndombe – founder of Soundwave, previously Senior Software Engineer at Pinterest and Netflix

3 Prizes Available:
- 1st place $500
- 2nd place $300
- 3rd place $200

honors.title: Chick-fil-A Leadership Scholarship
honors.description:
- $2,500 scholarship given to Chick-fil-A (CFA) employees that demonstrate leadership qualities and outstanding work ethic correlating to CFA specific values

- 7 applicants were chosen out of the total 15+ applicants

- Requirements to apply:
     - Be employed at a Chick-fil-A franchise at time of award
     - Be a postsecondary student at an accredited two or four-year college 
     - Be recommended by the Operator, Interim or Executive General Manager
     - Have active involvement in community service with the 12 months prior to application 
     - Minimum GPA of 2.5 - 4.0

projects.title: Wings - 2nd Place (National CodePath Demo Day June 2021)
projects.description:
A fully student run Android app project, collaborated with a team of 4 (named NSLJ) over the last six weeks of the CodePath Android Development course, ultimately winning 2nd Place at National CodePath Android Demo Day - 2021!

2nd Place Certificate here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AKBy2w06I_fsuSufYmBjdJmiDKD04hsA/view?usp=sharing

Technologies Used:
- Languages:   Java, XML
- Parse backend server, through back4app.com
- Google Maps SDK, Google Directions API
- GitHub
- Figma
- AndroidStudio IDE

Specific Contributions:
- #1 contributor:   71.91% of commits, 41.56% of additions, and 98.73% of deletions.
- Designed app frame through Google docs and Discord:  includes list of 20+ class files, 5 models, 6 screen archetypes, screen navigation, and Google API and Android resources
- Setup GitHub project board, including all 4 milestones and 13+ issues
- Updated status and addressed project issues biweekly through product sprint meetings
- Exclusively demoed the app on National CodePath Android Demo Day

Project Description:
Inspired by recent spikes of hate crimes, as well as the models of self-community applications such as Uber and DoorDash, Wings connects users to others when in alarming physical situations. 

It's often said, "It's better to walk in groups!"

Wings is an Android app whose main focus is pairing users who commonly need a "buddy" to walk with, to get to some common destination! However, generally, the app provides in the simplest case of any user needing physical help in real time! Prime examples include: automatically notifying trusted contacts at any time, automatic dialing of emergency services, registering for an escort, and providing the nearest registered safe spots!

projects.title: Numerical Methods Calculator
projects.description:
This is a 4-person group project created and completed for Cal Poly Pomona's CS 4080 - Concepts of Programming Languages course! 

The project displays a GUI-based calculator that allows the user to obtain answers to several numerical methods! Specifically, these algorithms are implemented: Newton-Raphson (finds roots), Lagrange Interpolation (approximates polynomials), and Gaussian Elimination (solves equations). 

Technologies Used:
- Python
- Tkinter (Python GUI Module!)
- PyCharm IDE

Specific Contributions:
- Exclusively implemented the Gaussian Forward Elimination w/ Back Substitution algorithm as an object class, taking any sized matrix of equations and variables. 
- Re-built the UI through re-organizing the GUI implementations of 3 numerical method functions into 3 groups of OOP associations.
